text: First proper week at Bakkerij Vos. Alarm at 4:40, which my body still treats as a personal insult. The ovens are already roaring when I walk in and the whole street smells of butter by six. I'm on rolls and krentenbollen for now, not trusted with the sourdough yet. Burned my wrist on a tray, nothing serious. Home by two, asleep on the sofa by three. Strange rhythm, but I like coming home with flour in my hair.

Femke came over with a bag of stroopwafels and we spent the whole afternoon assembling the bookcase I've been avoiding for a month. She reads instructions; I don't. Very on-brand for us since childhood. My sister still laughs exactly like Mum when something collapses, and something collapsed twice. Ended with takeaway noodles on the floor among the screws. Nice to have her ten minutes away again.

Watered everything this morning and the monstera has a new leaf unrolling, very slowly, like it's embarrassed. The basil on the windowsill is not doing well; too much sun or too little, I honestly can't tell. Moved it to the table. Talked to the plants a bit, which I will deny if anyone asks. Small green victories.

Sat down with all the bills that have been piling up on the hallway shelf. Energy went up again, of course. Internet is fine. Somehow I'm still paying for a streaming service I haven't opened since autumn, so that's cancelled now. Made a little spreadsheet and felt like an adult for about twenty minutes, then ate cereal for dinner.

Groceries at the supermarket near the station. Butter is absurd now, almost four euros. Bought the store-brand coffee out of protest and will probably regret it tomorrow morning. Leeks were cheap so it's soup season, whether I like it or not. Carried two heavy bags home in the wind and my fingers still have the plastic marks.

Went bouldering after my shift, forearms completely cooked. There's a new purple route on the overhang wall that I fell off maybe eight times. Got the top hold once and then just dangled there like laundry. Chalk everywhere, even in my ears somehow. Cycled home slowly in the dark, very happy and very hungry.

Repotted the spider plant that has been trying to escape its pot for weeks. Roots everywhere, soil all over the kitchen floor. The little babies hanging off it now have their own jars of water on the windowsill. If they all root I'll have to start giving plants away to people who didn't ask for them.

Pickle discovered the park pond today and simply walked in, without hesitation, like he'd been planning it for weeks. My dog has no sense of temperature. He came out shaking pond water all over a man on a bench, who was very gracious about it. Two towels, one bath, and now he's asleep on my feet smelling vaguely of duckweed.

Rain all evening, the sound on the skylight is the best thing about this flat. Made tea, lit the one candle I own, and watched the street lights blur. Didn't look at my phone for two hours, which felt almost suspicious. Wrote a few lines in this notebook and then just listened.

The screen on my Fairphone 4 has a crack across one corner now, from the tiles in the bakery, but it still works. I keep meaning to replace the screen myself since that's the whole point of the thing. Ordered the part; it comes with a tiny screwdriver. We'll see how brave I am.

Spent ages on the phone with the health insurance people about a bill that was sent twice. Twenty-five minutes of hold music, a very calm woman, and the problem was solved in two minutes. Celebrated by paying the actual bill immediately so I couldn't forget. Admin day done.

Second grocery run this week because I forgot eggs. The self-checkout yelled at me about an unexpected item in the bagging area, which was my own scarf. Bought tulips because they were two euros and the kitchen looks a lot better with them. Prices still make me wince.

The basil is officially dead. I've given it a quiet funeral in the compost bin. The monstera leaf is fully open now though, so the overall plant count is stable. Thinking of trying mint instead, which supposedly survives anything, including me.

Cleaned the leaves of the rubber plant with a damp cloth, one by one, which is weirdly meditative. It looks shiny and pleased with itself now. Noticed little gnats in one pot, so that's tomorrow's problem. Watered everything except the cactus, which judges me silently from the shelf.

Tomasz and I got stuck doing the delivery inventory together at work, counting flour sacks in the cold storage room and arguing about whether a half sack counts. My colleague has an opinion about everything, including the correct way to stack crates, but he's funny about it. We finished an hour late and shared the leftover appelflappen.

Train to Amersfoort was cancelled, then the next one was delayed, so I spent forty minutes on a cold platform reading the same news article three times. A pigeon walked over my shoe. Eventually got there, did the errand in ten minutes and turned straight back. Very efficient waste of a day.

Bought new running shoes, the Asics Novablast, after my old pair finally split at the sole. They're bright blue and bouncy, like running on marshmallows. Did a short loop along the canal to test them and my knees didn't complain once. Spent too much, but my shins will thank me.

The power went out in our whole building tonight. Ines knocked on my door with a camping lantern and a bottle of wine, so we sat on the stairs in the dark talking for two hours. My neighbour turns out to be a nurse on night shifts, which explains the odd hours. Lights came back on and we both felt a bit disappointed.

Finally set up automatic payments for rent so I stop panicking on the first of every month. Also found out I'm owed a small tax refund, which feels like finding money in a coat pocket. Put it straight into savings before I could think of something stupid to buy.

Found my place: Koffie Kantoor, a tiny spot near the Oudegracht with mismatched chairs and a barista who remembers my order after one visit. Their cardamom bun is unreasonable. Sat in the window for an hour with a book and didn't read a single page, just watched bikes go by. My favourite cafe now, officially.

Bouldering again tonight. Got the purple route on the overhang, finally, on the second try. Didn't even feel like I was trying, it just clicked. The gym was packed and somebody clapped, which was mortifying and lovely. Skin on my fingertips is shredded, worth it.

Kofi made jollof rice tonight and insisted I learn how so he doesn't have to cook it every single week. Apparently I stir wrong. We ate on the balcony even though it was freezing, because he says food tastes better outside. Living with a roommate who cooks this well is dangerous for my waistline.

Made the leek soup at last. Too much pepper, not enough salt, but with bread it was good. Froze four portions for future me, who will be grateful. The kitchen smells like onions for the rest of the evening and the windows steamed right up.
Watched three episodes of that Danish crime series in a row. Everyone is so sad and so well dressed. I guessed the killer wrong, again. Went to bed far too late with the theme music stuck in my head.

Went swimming at the indoor pool before work. Lane etiquette is a lawless place at seven in the morning. Did twenty lengths and felt like a fish for about five minutes, then like a tired person in goggles. The chlorine smell stayed on my skin all day.

Bouldering session cut short because I tweaked a finger on a crimpy route. Taped it up and just did easy slabs for the rest of the hour. Need to learn to stop when my hands say stop. Iced it at home with a bag of frozen peas.

Femke brought Biscotti along to the market this morning. Her dog's name suits him: small, crunchy-looking and sweet. He tried to eat a whole herring from the fish stall and got very offended when he wasn't allowed. Biscotti and my dog sniffed each other for ages and then decided they were best friends.

Ines gave me a lift to the garden centre in her car, an old yellow Fiat Panda with a dented door and a cassette player that actually works. We listened to some mixtape from the nineties on full volume. The Fiat Panda made a worrying noise on every roundabout but it got us there and back with a whole boot full of pots.

Gas bill came in lower than expected, so the tiny electric blanket strategy is working. Paid it, filed it, felt smug. Also renewed my bike insurance after reading every line of the small print, which was a bad idea for my mood.

Rain again, heavy this time, water running down the street like a little river. I stayed in with a puzzle of a lighthouse that's mostly grey sky. Found a corner piece under the sofa after twenty minutes of searching. Very satisfying, very small life.

Listened to a long podcast episode about the history of salt while cleaning the bathroom. Did not expect to care about salt this much. Apparently wars were fought over it. Now I keep looking at the salt shaker with new respect.

Errands in town: returned a library book three days late, bought batteries, got a key cut, and picked up a parcel from the corner shop. The shop owner gave me a free liquorice, which made the whole round worth it. Cycled home with the wind for once.

Tomasz finally took me to Bar Bolle, which he talks about constantly. It's his favourite cafe by a mile, dark wood, loud jazz, and a cheese toastie he claims is the best in Utrecht. He's not wrong about the toastie. He knows every barista by name and orders without looking at the menu.

Bouldering tonight with the finger fully healed. Worked on footwork drills like a responsible person, then threw myself at a dyno and missed by a mile. Landed badly on the mat, laughed, tried again, missed again. A good night anyway.

Tried to make shakshuka from memory and it came out more like spicy tomato soup with eggs floating in it. Still delicious with lots of bread. Burned the bottom of the pan, scrubbed for ages. Next time, less water, more patience.

First day at the Openbare Bibliotheek. Quiet, warm, smells of paper and floor polish, and nobody needs me at four in the morning anymore. I'm on the returns desk and shelving for now, learning the system. Lunch in the reading room overlooking the square. My new workplace feels like a deep breath.

Finished the Danish crime series. The ending was bleak and beautiful and I'm not over it. Immediately started a cooking competition show to recover. Somebody cried about a collapsed cake and honestly, same.

Kofi took me for a drive in his car, a gorgeous old grey Volvo Amazon that he restores bit by bit on weekends. No power steering, smells of leather and petrol, gets stared at at every traffic light. He drives it like it's made of glass. The Volvo Amazon is apparently older than both of us combined.

Swimming after work. The pool was nearly empty so I had a lane to myself and did thirty lengths, slow and steady. Floated on my back at the end looking at the ceiling lights. Best I've slept in weeks.

Bouldering with a sore back, so mostly traversing along the bottom of the wall. Tried a new blue problem, fell off the last move three times. The setters must hate short people. Still left in a good mood with chalky jeans.

Started a new series, some British comedy about a terrible hotel. Laughed out loud alone in the living room, which felt slightly unhinged. Ate crisps for dinner while watching, which I will not be recording as a balanced meal.

Another rainy night. Sat by the window with a hot water bottle and wrote letters I'll probably never send. The gutters overflowed and made a small waterfall past the glass. Cosy, a bit lonely, mostly fine.

Femke came over with a stack of old records she found at a flea market. Of course it was mostly Golden Earring, her favourite band since she was about twelve. She played Radar Love three times in a row and air-drummed on my kitchen table. I pretended to be annoyed and secretly loved it.

Baked banana bread with three very black bananas. The house smelled amazing for hours. It sank a bit in the middle, which I've decided is a feature. Ate two slices warm with butter, standing at the counter.

Got a new phone today, a Pixel 8. The camera is ridiculous, I took fifty photos of the dog in the first hour. Moving everything over took all evening and I lost half my chat history somewhere along the way. Still, no more cracked screen, and the battery lasts all day.

Terrible night. Woke at three with my brain listing every awkward thing I've said since 2014. Tried counting, tried reading, tried warm milk. Fell asleep at five, alarm at seven. Walked around like a ghost all day, drank too much coffee.
Made a big pot of chili and ate it three nights in a row. By the third night it was the best version, as chili always is. The kitchen still smells of cumin and I don't mind at all.

Moved the sofa to the other wall on a whim and the whole living room suddenly feels twice the size. Found two euros, a hair tie, and a lost earring underneath it. Rearranged the bookshelf by colour, which is impractical but makes me happy.

Another restless night, kept waking up hot and then cold. The street was loud with someone's party until two. Gave up at six and watched the sky go pink over the roofs. Napped at lunchtime with my head on the desk.

Long talk with Kofi tonight about growing up. He was born in Paramaribo and still calls it home, even after fifteen years here. He described the heat, the wooden houses, the river, his grandmother's kitchen. Paramaribo sounds loud and green and nothing like a grey Dutch March.

Bought mint at the market to replace the late basil. Planted it in a big pot so it can't take over the windowsill. Watered all the plants and noticed the spider plant babies have roots now. I am going to be giving plants away.

New running shoes today: the Hoka Clifton. They feel like clouds strapped to my feet, slightly silly-looking but very soft. Ran along the canal and back without my calves complaining once. My running shoes are honestly the only thing I'm happy to overspend on.

Bouldering on a quiet Tuesday night, nearly had the wall to myself. Finally flashed a route I'd never seen before, first try, no falls. Did a little victory dance on the mat that nobody saw. Perfect evening.

Started at Museum Speelklok today, the music box and street organ museum. The first hour I just stood there grinning while a huge organ played behind me. I'll be giving tours eventually; for now I'm learning which tiny cylinder plays which tune. Best workplace I've ever had, I think.

Bouldering after the museum, tired legs but happy hands. Worked on the blue problem that has been mocking me for weeks and finally got it. Celebrated with fries on the way home, eaten while walking in the drizzle.

Deep cleaned the flat: windows, oven, behind the fridge. Found an alarming amount of dust and one sock. Opened every window afterwards and let the cold air in. The whole place feels brand new, at least until tomorrow.

Listened to a podcast about people who walk across whole countries alone. Felt inspired, then remembered I get blisters walking to the station. Maybe a short walk along the river this weekend instead. Small ambitions.
Swimming early before work, cold water, warm afterwards. Managed my first proper flip turn without inhaling half the pool. Small achievement, unreasonably proud. Ate a huge breakfast after.

Slow afternoon at work, rain outside and hardly any visitors. Polished display cases, reorganised the brochure rack twice, and watched the clock. Drank three cups of tea. Some days are just for quietly getting through.
